name: facet_r2_draft
description: DRAFT R2 facet benchmark fixture (50 memories / 20 queries), grounded in REAL menhir + archolith-bench history rather than synthetic or public data: the R1 source-aware-floor change superseding the old cosine floor, the cth.mcp.memory→yawn_memory→menhir rename chain, the documented CE-willow belief drift (belief-layer.md E1–E5), real files/symbols/bugs, and genuine cross-repo collisions (both repos talk about BM25/floor/RRF/meet-point). NEEDS ADVERSARIAL HARDENING WITH ctharvey (R2 Risk #1, 'fixture too clean'): tighten distractors, confirm gold support IDs, add harder paraphrases. Validate with archolith_bench.facet.validate before trusting any run.

memories.text: Fixed the menhir recall floor so BM25-found candidates are no longer cut by the cosine similarity threshold. The source-aware floor now gates only VECTOR candidates in recall_service.py and scoring_service.py. As of 2026-06-20 this is current behavior.

Previously the menhir recall floor in recall_service.py applied a single cosine similarity threshold to every candidate, which silently cut BM25 matches. This was the approach before the source-aware floor.
The menhir scoring_service floor is now source-aware: it gates only VECTOR candidates and exempts BM25, pending, and file-linked sources via FLOOR_EXEMPT_SOURCES in scoring_service.py.
Added weighted_rrf in hybrid_retrieval.py to blend the vector and BM25 passes on rank instead of raw score, avoiding the BM25/cosine scale mismatch.
Rejected the linear alpha*cosine + (1-alpha)*bm25 blend for menhir retrieval because the BM25 and cosine score scales do not match; rank fusion was chosen instead.
Added search_ranked_by_method to graphiti_client.py for per-method ranked passes; search_scored is unchanged and still the default recall path. This is the symbol rename/expansion case.
menhir CandidateSource and SOURCE_PRIORS in retrieval_tuning.py formalize the old ad-hoc 1.0/0.3 injected priors so BM25/facet/structure candidates carry an explicit prior and survive the floor.
menhir hybrid_alpha ships at a neutral 0.5 as a seam, not a tuned value; archolith-bench is expected to tune it via a sweep over 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1.0.
The menhir similarity floor constant MIN_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD defaults to 0.15 in scoring_service.py, but whether that is on the right scale versus live Graphiti RRF scores is still unverified.
menhir graphiti_client search_scored runs a hybrid BM25 + cosine node search and reranks with RRF; it remains the default retrieval path.
The project was originally named cth.mcp.memory, a Neo4j-backed memory graph service for agent context.
The project was renamed from cth.mcp.memory to yawn_memory; the Python package became src/yawn_memory.
The project is now named menhir; the Python package is src/menhir and the console script is `menhir serve`. This is the current name.
menhir configuration environment variables use the MENHIR_ prefix, for example MENHIR_BACKEND_URL and MENHIR_API_KEY in settings.py.
menhir config environment variables used to use the YAWN_MEMORY_ prefix (for example YAWN_MEMORY_BACKEND_URL) before the rename to menhir.
Observed the original Combat Extended (CE) willow texture-cache crash in the modded game session.
Added the CE willow patch to address the texture-cache crash.
At the time it appeared the CE willow patch fully fixed the crash. This was believed then but later narrowed once the load-order issue surfaced — it should not be asserted as current truth.
A compatibility / load-order issue appeared after the CE willow patch; the crash was not fully resolved.
The load-order fix resolved the remaining CE willow compatibility issue. This is the current explanation for what fixed the problem.

AnergicBeliefGate suppresses a semantically relevant but stale or superseded memory from current-truth retrieval and assertion, while preserving it for historical and conflict traversal. Owned by belief.py.
The belief recall buckets were expanded: the coarse do_not_assert bucket split into HISTORICAL_ONLY, ANERGIC_CURRENT, and BLOCKED so superseded-but-useful memories are not mixed with unsafe ones.
The v1 do_not_assert bucket was a single coarse bucket that mixed historically useful superseded memories with unsafe or noisy ones. This was replaced by the finer bucket split.
archolith-bench BM25 baseline uses Okapi BM25 with k1=1.5 and b=0.75 over memory text for the retrieval ladder.
archolith-bench MeetPointReranker computes a meet_score over facet convergence with stale and wrong-scope penalties, and emits a per-candidate explanation trace.
archolith-bench applies a score floor to drop weak candidates before scoring in the benchmark harness; rank_from_scores discards zero-score documents.
archolith-bench rrf_fuse performs reciprocal-rank fusion of several ranked id lists, fusing on rank not raw score.
archolith-bench LongMemEval adapter runs the official long-term memory QA benchmark as a direct-vs-proxy A/B with a deterministic normalized scorer.

menhir scheduler_lease force_acquire overwrites the lease row without first stopping the previous owner, so concurrent scheduler loops can overlap until the old owner notices lease loss. Known defect.
menhir CircuitBreaker implements a CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN state machine on the Graphiti backends to stop hammering a failing LLM endpoint.
menhir EmbeddingCache is a SHA256-keyed LRU cache at the OpenAI-compatible client layer to avoid re-embedding identical text.
menhir Neo4j defaults are bolt://localhost:7687 with password 'password' and no forced encryption; safe for local dev but unsafe as a production posture.
menhir enforces rolling-window LLM budget caps per session with retry_after requeue semantics so a single session cannot exhaust the model budget.
menhir deferred enrichment runs as an in-process asyncio worker with journal-first writes; episode state is durable in Neo4j and failure history is appended in SQLite.
menhir ContextBuilderService packs recall results into a token budget with a tiktoken-or-heuristic fallback before handing context to the model.
menhir ingest_project scans a repo and writes deterministic structural entities (project, directory, file, symbol) plus CONTAINS/IMPORTS/CALLS/DEFINES/TESTS edges directly into Neo4j.

menhir structural_anchoring links semantic entities to structural entities via ANCHORED_TO, and recall can inject file-linked candidates through file_context even when vector similarity alone would miss them.
menhir query_structure exposes projects, overview, files, imports, symbols, blast_radius, and affected_tests over the pre-indexed structural graph.
menhir :Todo nodes are stored directly in Neo4j as operator-managed work items; they bypass Graphiti, decay, and semantic recall, and link via REFERENCES_FILE / CREATED_FROM / CONCERNS.
menhir incremental project diff compares stored file_mtime values on re-scan and only deletes and rewrites symbols for changed files; hot_count tracks how often each file changes.
menhir lifecycle decay moves memories ACTIVE -> COMPRESSED -> GONE with LLM compression and rehydration in lifecycle_service.py.
menhir conflict governance builds conflict groups with LLM contradiction confirmation; has_conflict and conflict_status flow into scoring, and the conflict preset uses delta=0.4.
menhir session->persistent consolidation promotes SESSION-scoped memories to PERSISTENT on consolidate and runs contradiction detection during promotion.
menhir recall is a two-phase pipeline: Graphiti vector search (search_scored) then graph-based scoring with relevance = similarity + alpha*adjacency + beta*recency + gamma*prominence.
menhir sage-wiki integration connected the memory graph to the workspace wiki so recall includes wiki documentation context (completed 2026-04-14).
Honestly the whole recall experience felt sluggish and grindy today — like it churned through far too much before returning anything useful.
Debugging the scheduler was maddening this afternoon; I kept going in circles and getting nowhere.
All 12 menhir v1 milestones (M0 through M7 plus the half-steps) shipped on 2026-03-18 with 722+ tests passing.
menhir exposes 23 MCP tools across ingest, recall, conflict, and ops, plus read-only resources for Claude Code.
menhir telemetry persists to a SQLite sidecar at <workspace_root>/.agent/mcp_telemetry.db resolved by infrastructure/paths.py, recording operation timings and structured failures.
